newsitem.title: MALI: Mali sets July dates for parliamentary poll rerun.
newsitem.headline: Mali sets July dates for parliamentary poll rerun.

text.p: The West African state of Mali has set July 6 and 20 as the dates for a rerun of April's chaotic parliamentary election, which was annulled by the constitutional court.
A cabinet statement issued on Wednesday night said campaigning for the first round would open on June 15.
The constitutional court ruled last month that numerous irregularities had flawed the April 13 first-round vote for the former French colony's 147-seat parliament.
Opposition parties are still demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Ibrahim Keita and the dissolution of the electoral commission.
They boycotted the May 11 presidential election which saw the incumbent Alpha Oumar Konare win 84 percent of votes in the first round.

Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system. Military leader Amadou Toumani Toure stepped down after 14 months and now often mediates in regional political crises.
